definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Name the syntactic or punctuation feature (repetition and commas, voice, hyphen, capitals, sentence type) and explain what it does to the meaning, emphasis or reader of the sentence. definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Judge or explain what the opening move or rhetorical question does for the reader and the writer's purpose, tying it to the text's intention. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
subject: english
required_knowledge: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Opening and rhetorical devices in the batch are a rhetorical question, an opening sentence whose appropriateness is judged, and a rhetorical question whose effectiveness is explained. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
prerequisites: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Recognise the device and locate it at the start of the text or paragraph. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
required_reasoning: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Explain what the device does for the reader and the writer's purpose, not merely what a rhetorical question is. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
required_procedure: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Name the device and where it occurs; state its effect on the reader; connect it to the writer's purpose or the column's argument. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
evidence_of_understanding: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] An effect of the opening move tied to the writer's purpose in this text. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
marking_requirements: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] The memoranda credit effect and purpose: the 2016 memo judges the opening sentence by its conversational style, its use of a quotation and the writer's purpose of raising awareness; the 2017 memo explains that the opening question points to the ridiculousness of the question and involves the reader; the 2018 memo credits a rhetorical question with raising awareness and prompting action. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
misconceptions: [Tier 3 possible belief, not observed] The definition of the rhetorical device is offered instead of its effect. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
